geo.label: March lift-off priced; war premium rising
parts: Macro Stance

The US story has shifted from rates alone to rates plus a geopolitical risk premium, and that pairing is hostile to equity multiples. Reuters reported consumer prices posting their largest annual gain in 40 years as inflation became widespread [[n2118]], while activity is not cracking: The Real Economy Blog charted industrial production rebounding [[n2150]] and housing permits at a 15-year high [[n2161]]. That leaves the Fed little room to soften into a war scare. The S&P 500 fell 2.12% to 4,380.26 index points and the VIX jumped 3.82 points to 28.11 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), the session Al Jazeera described as US stocks taking a hit as the Ukraine crisis stoked fear [[n0964]]. We are Bearish on broad US risk: growth is fine, but the cost of holding it is rising.
Rates & Curve

The 2Y closed at 1.49% and the 10Y at 1.97%, a 10Y-2Y spread of +48 bps on a curve that remains positively sloped (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-17). Over 20 observations the 2Y is up 41 bps and the 10Y up 14 bps, a 27 bps compression that the curve record labels bear flattening (both up, 2Y up more). The five-observation window tells the newer story: since 2022-02-10 the 2Y is down 12 bps and the 10Y down 6 bps, a haven bid layered on top of a hiking cycle. Reuters described the curve as pricing Fed tightening while showing fears of policy error [[n2217]], and Bloomberg warned that Treasury market liquidity is eroding with the Fed's course a gamble [[n2214]]. Thin liquidity means front-end moves can overshoot both ways.
New / Most Important

The January minutes did not lock in a pace: Reuters read them as showing a Fed not wed to any particular speed of hikes [[n2223]], while Al Jazeera stressed readiness to move faster if inflation persists [[n1385]]. The Fed's James Bullard again called for a front-loaded campaign, WSJ reported [[n1392]], and a Reuters poll still had 25 bps in March with calls for 50 bps growing louder [[n1376]]. Mortgage rates at 3.92%, the highest in 33 months according to the Orange County Register [[n2170]], show tightening already reaching housing. Add President Biden's warning, carried by PBS, of a very high risk of a Russian invasion in the next several days [[n1532]], and markets must price a hawkish Fed and a war premium at once.
Playbook ✓

Action: keep an underweight in long-duration growth, with the Nasdaq 100 at 14,171.74 index points and -4.54% over 20 sessions, funded into pricing-power staples and energy, and hold a gold hedge with gold at 1,902.00 USD/oz (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Trigger to add risk: a VIX close back below its 20-session-earlier 25.59 index points while the 2Y holds near 1.49%, which would show the haven bid fading without a hawkish repricing. What changes the call: if the 2Y retraces its five-observation decline while the VIX stays elevated, both the Fed and the war premium are tightening at once; then cut equity beta further.

geo.label: ECB gradualism meets a gas shock
parts: Macro Stance

Europe carries the purest version of the stagflation trade: closer to the conflict, more exposed to gas and served by a central bank that has promised to move slowly. ECB President Christine Lagarde repeated her pledge of a gradual policy shift, Reuters reported [[n1308]], and Bloomberg quoted her saying the ECB will act at the right time but only gradually [[n1315]]. The STOXX 600 closed at 464.55 index points, -3.89% over 20 sessions, a deeper slide than the S&P 500's -2.29% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Bearish.
Activity & Inflation

Inflation pressure is broadening rather than peaking. Reuters reported UK inflation climbing to 5.5%, the highest since 1992 [[n1353]], while a Reuters poll had the ECB lifting its deposit rate to -0.25% by year-end [[n1307]]. Energy is the swing factor: Dutch TTF gas jumped 7.33% to 74.91 EUR/MWh in one session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), after the Luxembourg Times reported European energy prices jumping on Ukraine tension [[n1310]]. Reuters set out Europe's options in case of a Russian gas disruption [[n1335]], a reminder that supply, not demand, is setting the price, and a supply-driven gas spike is a margin tax that rate policy cannot offset.
New / Most Important

The market is already discriminating by proximity. Raiffeisen Bank International fell 12.03% and Societe Generale 10.30% over five sessions, against a 1.65% decline for the STOXX 600 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Reuters reported that EU leaders would not discuss Russia sanctions at Thursday's meeting [[n1513]], leaving the sanctions template undefined, which is precisely the uncertainty banks seen as exposed to the region cannot hedge. The FTSE 100, at 7,537.40 index points and only -0.63% over 20 sessions, is the regional outlier because its energy and mining weight partly hedges the shock.
Playbook ✓

Action: stay underweight European cyclicals and banks, preferring staples with pricing power; Nestle told Reuters it is confident cost inflation will not bite margins [[n0931]]. Trigger to cover: TTF fully reversing its one-session 7.33% jump while bank losses stop extending. What changes the call: a credible de-escalation that pulls gas lower would make European banks the highest-beta rebound in the region.

geo.label: PBOC easing against trade and property drag
parts: Macro Stance

China is the one major economy where policy is leaning the other way, and that divergence is the core of our Mixed stance. Al Jazeera reported the central bank chief vowing support amid weak links [[n0251]], Bloomberg had the PBOC pumping in more liquidity and spurring gains in Chinese stocks [[n0228]], and Reuters reported that slowing inflation leaves room for policy easing [[n0235]]. Against that, external friction is rising and the property-credit tail has not been cut off. Markets are pricing the easing without pricing a reacceleration: the Shanghai Composite closed at 3,468.04 index points, -2.45% over 20 sessions, while the Hang Seng gained 2.37% to 24,792.77 index points over the same horizon (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17).
PMIs & Activity

Activity entered 2022 with a soft handoff. Reuters reported the Caixin survey showing factory activity contracting in January as COVID lockdowns bit [[n0179]]. The 2021 base was strong, with Global Times reporting GDP growth of 8.1%, the fastest in a decade [[n0163]], but Macau Business put fixed-asset investment up just 4.9 pct for the year [[n0165]], the clearest sign that the property drag was already weighing on capex. China Daily reported industrial profits rebounding in 2021 as production improved [[n0177]]. The mix argues for a recovery led by policy-directed infrastructure and manufacturing rather than consumers, while zero-COVID constraints persist: BBC reported Hong Kong's hospitals overwhelmed amid a spike in cases [[n0254]].
Credit Impulse

Credit is where easing should show first. CNBC reported the central bank cutting key lending rates in January, including one for the first time in nearly 2 years [[n0169]], and Fibre2Fashion reported cuts to medium-term loan and reverse repo rates [[n0172]]. Bloomberg framed it as the PBOC seizing the moment for stimulus while the Fed hikes [[n0174]]. The constraint is local-government leverage: the South China Morning Post reported Beijing telling banks to support rural infrastructure but not to add to hidden debt [[n0217]]. That is a deliberately narrow impulse channelled into approved projects, so the next credit print matters more for its composition, corporate medium-term lending versus short bills, than for its headline size.
Property

Property policy is easing at the margin, not pivoting. The Khmer Times reported that affordable rental housing is being excluded from property credit controls [[n0249]], a targeted carve-out rather than a rescue. Business Recorder reported December new home prices falling less on promotions and easing curbs [[n0160]]. Stress is still surfacing elsewhere in the credit chain: Bloomberg, citing Caixin, reported that Cedar was unable to pay $3.1 billion overdue [[n0218]], the kind of non-payment that keeps foreign high-yield buyers away from Chinese issuers generally. The sector is moving from free fall toward managed decline; that supports materials and banks at the margin but not a developer-equity rally.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Fiscal support is being steered into infrastructure, which China Briefing detailed as the main growth lever for 2022 [[n0191]]. The trade front is deteriorating. BBC reported Washington accusing China of serious harm to workers through its trade practices [[n0264]], and the Peterson Institute found China bought none of the extra $200 billion of US exports in Trump's trade deal [[n0185]]. CNN reported the US accusing Tencent and Alibaba of letting sellers traffic fake goods [[n0274]], and Reuters reported EU anti-dumping tariffs on Chinese steel fasteners [[n0271]]. Beijing is also policing commodities: Reuters reported China urging some iron ore traders to reduce inventory [[n0074]], a signal that it will lean against raw-material inflation rather than let a stimulus impulse become a price spike.
Markets & Flows

Offshore internet is where sentiment turned first. Tencent closed at 454.94 HKD, +5.99% over 20 sessions, while Alibaba's Hong Kong line fell 4.28% to 123.00 HKD and Xiaomi lost 10.59% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Business Insider reported Tencent joining the list of the world's ten most valuable companies as Meta slid [[n0873]], and CNBC reported banks from Credit Suisse to Goldman Sachs saying it is time to buy Chinese stocks [[n0237]]. Positioning is selective: Caixin Global reported Hillhouse gobbling up shares in NEV makers while ditching Alibaba and Bilibili [[n0638]]. Reuters reported the yuan slipping as divergent China-US monetary policy exerted pressure [[n0244]], the natural cost of easing into a Fed hiking cycle; a softer currency helps exporters only while commodity prices cooperate.
New / Most Important

The key development is that policy intent and external risk are now both explicit. The central bank chief's pledge of support [[n0251]] arrives as Washington sharpens its trade rhetoric, with PBS reporting US officials saying China's aggressive trade policies cause serious harm [[n0263]]. In parallel, Hong Kong's Omicron wave is testing zero-COVID: Al Jazeera reported President Xi telling Hong Kong to control the outbreak [[n0266]]. Easing, trade friction and COVID containment pull in different directions, which is why the Hang Seng's 20-session gain has not been matched by the US-listed FXI, down 3.18% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17).
Playbook ✓

Action: own Hong Kong-listed internet leaders selectively, Tencent over Alibaba, as the cleanest expression of easing, and avoid property-linked credit and US-listed EV names such as NIO, -15.14% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Trigger to add: the Hang Seng holding above its 20-session-earlier 24,218.03 index points while the next credit print shows a rising share of corporate medium-term loans. What changes the call: a new US enforcement step against platforms, or a Hong Kong lockdown that spills into mainland supply chains, would turn the internet trade into a funding source. ⚠ Divergence: monetary policy is easing and offshore tech is rallying, yet the Shanghai Composite is down over 20 sessions and the yuan is softening; markets believe the PBOC's intent more than its transmission.

geo.label: BOJ anchor intact, board turnover ahead
parts: Macro Stance

Japan is recovering, but imported energy costs rather than domestic demand are setting the pace. Reuters reported the economy rebounding on solid spending while Omicron clouds the outlook [[n1562]]. The policy question is flexibility: Reuters also reported that a board reshuffle may open scope for a less dovish BOJ [[n1570]]. That is a slow-moving catalyst, but it matters because the BOJ is the last major anchor holding down global term premia. The Nikkei 225 closed at 27,232.87 index points, -0.83% on the session and -0.85% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), a far shallower drawdown than the Nasdaq 100 that reflects Japan's light weighting in long-duration growth. Mixed.
Activity & Currency

The external account is the pressure point. Al Jazeera reported January exports growing less than expected as the trade deficit soared [[n1580]], after The Seattle Times reported imports hitting record highs on surging energy prices [[n1537]]. An energy-driven deficit is a structural headwind for the yen, and a weaker currency imports more inflation into a central bank that wants to stay patient. Industry is split. Automotive Logistics reported Toyota cutting March production plans because of the chip shortage [[n1954]], and Toyota fell 6.77% over five sessions to 2,160.50 JPY, while chip-equipment makers rallied, with Tokyo Electron +3.72% to 58,220.00 JPY and Advantest +4.50% to 9,760.00 JPY over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Asahi Shimbun reported TSMC expanding its new Japan chip factory with Denso taking a stake [[n1573]], anchoring that equipment demand at home. SoftBank Group's 8.82% five-session slide to 5,117.00 JPY shows the global growth de-rating reaching Tokyo through its tech-investment proxy.
Playbook ✓

Action: within Japan, favour semiconductor equipment over autos, and keep currency hedges on for foreign holders while the energy deficit widens. Trigger: Tokyo Electron extending its five-session gain while Toyota stays below its 20-session-earlier 2,303.00 JPY confirms the split. What changes the call: a clear signal from the reshaped BOJ board toward less accommodation would lift the yen and pressure exporters; then lift hedges and narrow the auto underweight.

geo.label: RBA patient while the Fed tightens
parts: Macro Stance

Australia's central bank is openly declining to follow the Fed, which keeps the domestic rate story benign even as inflation runs hot. WSJ reported the RBA's Harper backing a review and the central bank refusing to follow the Fed on rate increases [[n0082]]. The AFR had flagged a shock inflation spike to 3.5 per cent [[n0009]], and The Australian reported the jobless rate at a 13-year low as a hike loomed [[n0004]]. The S&P/ASX 200 closed at 7,296.20 index points, +0.16% in the 2022-02-17 session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), a session that ended before the US sell-off. Mixed.
Demand & Financing

Earnings show a two-speed economy. ABC News reported Fortescue Metals and CSL posting weaker profits under COVID restrictions [[n0052]], yet CSL rallied 9.18% over five sessions to 277.00 AUD while Fortescue fell 7.99% to 20.50 AUD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). The difference is China: Reuters reported Beijing urging iron ore traders to cut inventory [[n0074]], which lands directly on pure-play miners, while BHP's first-half profit beat estimates and triggered M&A talk, Reuters reported [[n0449]]. Rio Tinto, +9.13% over 20 sessions at 119.94 AUD, shows diversified miners holding up. Consumer-facing earnings are softer: Reuters reported profit dipping at Wesfarmers after a perfect pandemic storm [[n0784]]. Households also face rising rents, which the AFR called a possible sleeper factor for inflation [[n0026]].
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer diversified miners and healthcare, BHP and CSL, over iron-ore pure plays such as Fortescue. Trigger: Fortescue failing to hold its 20-session-earlier 20.44 AUD while Beijing keeps leaning on traders. What changes the call: an RBA shift toward following the Fed would hit rate-sensitive lenders such as Commonwealth Bank of Australia, at 98.81 AUD, and housing-linked consumption first.

geo.label: NBP hiking into 9% inflation on NATO's front line
parts: Macro Stance

Poland combines one of Europe's sharpest inflation problems with its most direct exposure to the Ukraine crisis, and markets are charging for both. Forsal.pl, citing GUS, reported January inflation at 9.2% [[n1756]]; the individual investors' association SII noted it came in below 10% after all but was still the highest this century [[n1758]]. The Monetary Policy Council is responding: Rzeczpospolita reported the RPP raising rates to their highest in almost nine years [[n1656]], and TheBanker profiled the central bank governor taking aim at inflation [[n1627]]. Growth is holding up, with TVN24 reporting GDP rising in the latest data [[n1644]], but Rzeczpospolita warned that a slowdown is being masked by statistics as inflation and rates already curb appetites [[n1645]]. We are Bearish: the hiking cycle is chasing inflation rather than leading it, and the geopolitical premium is rising.
Markets

Polish assets are trading as the front-line proxy. The iShares MSCI Poland ETF (EPOL) fell 3.70% to 20.58 USD in its last session and is down 4.81% over 20 sessions, while the Beta ETF WIG20TR lost 2.11% to 37.35 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Bankier.pl reported earlier in the week that the złoty was recovering losses even as the Ukrainian question hit markets [[n1738]], a sign of how quickly the currency swings with headlines. Money.pl reported gold prices rising and Ukrainian companies losing ground as the conflict escalated [[n1814]], and Parkiet asked how markets would react if a global armed conflict broke out [[n1791]]; that question is now part of the risk premium. Bank Pekao fell 3.70% to 130.25 PLN and PGE 4.55% to 7.59 PLN in one session, while Dino Polska rose 1.02% to 296.00 PLN, the defensive grocer outperforming the state-linked utility and the lender.
Fiscal & Politics

Fiscal policy is caught between the anti-inflation shield and the backlash against Polski Ład. Bankier.pl reported the Finance Ministry's estimated 2021 central-budget deficit at 26.3 billion zł [[n1670]], and Rzeczpospolita noted that inflation is helping the government manage state debt [[n1655]]. The bill is arriving elsewhere: 300Gospodarka.pl reported that pension indexation will cost more than the budget assumed because the index is higher [[n1681]]. Politically, Polski Ład has become a liability. Business Insider Polska reported that Jan Sarnowski, the official responsible for it, lost his post [[n1669]], Interia ran a poll on whether the reform hurt Law and Justice [[n1728]], and Next Gazeta.pl reported President Andrzej Duda now wants comprehensive changes, possibly a Polski Ład 2.0 [[n1779]]. On Europe, Rzeczpospolita reported the EU Court of Justice confirming the money-for-rule-of-law mechanism as Ziobro attacked Morawiecki [[n1801]], and BBC framed it as Hungary and Poland losing their EU funding fight [[n1615]]. EU money stays conditional, a direct risk to the medium-term investment story.
Corporate & Sectors

Corporate news is dominated by energy security and cost pass-through. Biznes Alert quoted Woźniak rejecting any new Yamal contract with Russia [[n1736]], while the energy regulator URE reported a record price for natural gas imported from EU countries in the fourth quarter of 2021 [[n1730]], costs that regulated tariffs may not fully pass on. That helps explain PGE's 5.65% and Tauron's 5.55% declines over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). WysokieNapiecie.pl reported Rafako moving only slowly on coke work for JSW [[n1822]]; JSW fell 5.23% to 44.55 PLN in one session yet remains +10.55% over 20 sessions on coking-coal prices. Nuclear is the long-run answer: POWER Magazine reported Poland securing a NuScale SMR [[n1605]] and eKoszalin reported KGHM targeting small modular reactors in Poland by 2029 [[n1763]]. Among consumer names, Strefa Biznesu reported Biedronka raising pay [[n1781]] and DlaHandlu.pl reported Aldi, Biedronka, Dino and Lidl hiring almost 2300 people [[n1796]], so discounters are absorbing wage inflation. CD Projekt released its next-generation Cyberpunk 2077 update and free trial, per its investor relations site [[n1744]], but Eurogamer.pl reported gamers disappointed by 30 FPS on Xbox Series S [[n1816]]; the stock is -5.26% over 20 sessions at 180.00 PLN.
Geopolitics & Security

Poland's security posture has hardened visibly. Reuters reported the US sending 3,000 additional troops to Poland [[n1594]], The National Interest reported additional US F-15s sent to bolster NATO's eastern flank [[n1625]], and Notes From Poland reported a trilateral Ukraine-UK-Poland agreement in the face of Russian aggression [[n1629]]. Diplomacy is strained: TVN24 quoted Rau, after talks with Lavrov, saying European security is in deep crisis [[n1772]], Interia confirmed the head of Poland's foreign ministry was in Moscow for those talks [[n1773]], and Interia separately reported Russian diplomat Maria Zakharova claiming the Polish government acts in US rather than national interests [[n1815]]. Donald Tusk said the situation in Ukraine will decide whether Poland is safe, PolsatNews.pl reported [[n1826]]. On the Belarus border, wnp.pl reported barrier construction running on three shifts [[n1820]], and CNBC reported US troops in Poland preparing to help refugees if Russia invades [[n1600]], making a refugee flow a live fiscal and labour-market variable.
New / Most Important

The decisive input is the interaction between rate hikes and the risk premium. Hikes should support bank net interest income, and mBank is +3.43% over 20 sessions at 470.00 PLN, yet the same lenders are first to be sold on geopolitical headlines, with PKO Bank Polski -3.43% and Pekao -4.37% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). The SII reported that rates are up again and that the central bank has not said its last word [[n1657]], so the earnings tailwind is intact. Gazeta Prawna reported Swiss-franc mortgage cases falling off court calendars as claims expand [[n1824]], which prolongs a legal overhang on the same banks.
Playbook ✓

Action: stay underweight Polish equities through EPOL and WIG20 exposure, preferring domestic defensives such as Dino over utilities and lenders until the geopolitical premium eases. Trigger to turn constructive: EPOL reclaiming its 20-session-earlier 21.62 USD while the złoty stabilises and the next CPI print signals a peak; then rotate into PKO Bank Polski and mBank for rate-hike earnings leverage. What changes the call: a military escalation or a new Belarus-border incident would extend the drawdown regardless of rates. ⚠ Divergence: the hiking cycle is a powerful earnings tailwind for Polish banks, yet they are leading the sell-off; rate leverage says buy, front-line risk says wait.
Narrative

Technology is splitting between visible-demand hardware and narrative-dependent software. XLK fell 2.99% to 154.00 USD and is -2.20% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), even as five-observation yields eased, so this is not a pure discount-rate trade.
Reported

Cisco raised its annual earnings forecast and announced $15 bln of share buybacks, Reuters reported [[n1184]], and CNBC's Investing Club called it a beat and raise that defied the doubters [[n1196]]; the stock rose 2.80% to 55.77 USD. Salesforce fell 5.53% and Microsoft 2.93% on the same session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17).
EPS Upside Watch

Intel's roadmap is the long-dated upside test: The Next Platform reported it unfolding a Xeon roadmap with more cores and denser transistors [[n2024]], and Fast Company described Pat Gelsinger's audacious $43.5B revival plan [[n0911]]. Upside depends on execution years out, which is why Intel slipped 1.37% rather than rallying.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention says falling yields rescue software multiples. Not on this tape: yields fell and software still sold, because investors are paying for cash returns and dated catalysts rather than duration. Buybacks, not total addressable market, are the scarce asset, and Cisco's reception proves it.
Narrative

Communication services is the epicentre of the growth de-rating. XLC closed at 67.94 USD, -9.11% over 20 sessions, and Meta Platforms (FB) is -34.39% over the same span at 207.71 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Bloomberg reported Meta losing its top-10 market-value ranking amid its worst month ever [[n0929]].
Reported

Roku's revenue missed on supply-chain snags and shares fell 20%, Reuters reported [[n0949]]. Reuters also reported Paramount shares slumping as investment to beef up streaming spooked investors [[n0780]], and Deadline put the drop at nearly 20% [[n0815]].
EPS Upside Watch

Upside now depends on cost discipline, because the market punishes content and metaverse spending. Spotify's -23.69% and Netflix's -23.92% 20-session losses (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17) show streaming multiples compressing; Forbes reported Joe Rogan's Spotify deal allegedly worth $200 million [[n2027]], the kind of commitment investors now scrutinise.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Platforms are supposed to be quality compounders that trade together. Snap's +12.75% 20-session gain against Pinterest's -22.72% shows dispersion inside the group now exceeds the sector move; this is a stock-picker's tape, not a sector bet. Alphabet Class A's 3.77% drop to 2,650.78 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17) shows even the highest-quality ad franchise is not immune on risk-off days.
Narrative

Financials should benefit from hikes, but bear flattening caps the payoff. XLF fell 2.49% to 39.23 USD, while the 10Y-2Y spread has compressed 27 bps over 20 observations to +48 bps (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17; US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-17).
Reported

Bank of America's CEO told Reuters the capital-markets business is down but pipelines are full [[n0861]]. Goldman Sachs lifted its financial targets in a bid to win over sceptics, Reuters reported [[n0901]], though the Financial Times saw new targets with the same existential angst [[n0902]].
EPS Upside Watch

Net interest income is the lever if long yields rise faster than short ones; for now the opposite is happening. Insurers are steadier: Reuters reported AIG's profit beating estimates on general insurance strength [[n1182]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The worst bank performance is about conduct, not credit. Morgan Stanley fell 10.62% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17) after WSJ reported regulators probing block trading at Morgan Stanley, Goldman and other Wall Street firms [[n0481]], and Reuters reported Morgan Stanley's Archegos role sped up those probes [[n0771]].
Narrative

Energy remains the cleanest hedge against inflation and geopolitics at once. XLE is +7.47% over 20 sessions at 68.47 USD with Brent at 92.97 USD/bbl and WTI at 91.76 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Reuters reported oil hitting seven-year highs as markets feared a Russian attack [[n0120]].
Reported

Supply discipline holds: Middle East Eye reported Saudi Arabia rejecting a US request to raise output [[n1362]], and Reuters reported an IEA demand revision confirming a tighter market [[n0523]]. Norway's oil firms hiked 2022 investment plans, Reuters reported [[n0936]].
EPS Upside Watch

Henry Hub gas at 4.49 USD/MMBtu, +17.99% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), adds a second earnings leg for producers. CNBC reported Warren Buffett increasing an energy bet by more than a third [[n0486]], long-horizon capital endorsing the cash-flow case.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The threat to the trade is diplomacy, not demand. Reuters reported the Iran nuclear deal draft puts prisoners, enrichment and cash first and oil later [[n1514]], so a deal would not release barrels immediately; energy longs can be held through Iranian headlines.
Narrative

Industrials are caught between strong orders and rising freight and input costs. XLI fell 1.83% to 99.16 USD, Caterpillar is -10.10% over 20 sessions at 194.74 USD and Deere fell 2.57% to 380.53 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Bloomberg warned that the US freight cost blowout may mean little inflation relief soon [[n1574]].
Reported

Airbus is flying high with $4.8 billion record net income and pulling away from Boeing, AirGuide Business reported [[n2010]], but WSJ reported that its plan to ramp up production of its bestselling jet hit snags [[n0852]]. Reuters reported the US will inspect new 787 Dreamliners because Boeing cannot self-certify [[n0675]].
EPS Upside Watch

Defence is the quiet beneficiary: Northrop Grumman is +4.21% over five sessions and Raytheon Technologies (RTX) +6.79% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Reuters reported Lockheed scrapping its $4.4 billion Aerojet deal amid regulatory roadblocks [[n0491]], freeing capital for buybacks.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Strong demand is not protecting margins. FreightWaves reported U.S. Xpress seeing freight moving at fever pitch [[n2157]]; volume is there, but cost pass-through, not order books, now decides which industrials re-rate.
Narrative

Discretionary is losing the inflation tug-of-war. XLY fell 2.68% to 181.12 USD and Tesla 5.09% to 876.35 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), and Yahoo Finance reported US consumers in a deep funk [[n2125]].
Reported

DoorDash is the exception: Reuters reported revenue beating as the food-delivery boom continued, with shares soaring 24% [[n0732]]; by the regular-session close the gain was 10.69%. CNBC reported Airbnb beating on earnings with strong guidance [[n0544]].
EPS Upside Watch

Pricing is the lever. CBS News reported Chipotle planning to hike menu prices again, citing inflation [[n1095]], and Forbes reported Louis Vuitton raising prices worldwide on higher costs [[n0618]]. Chipotle still fell 4.16% to 1,509.86 USD, showing investors doubt price can fully offset volume.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Tesla's discount is regulatory, not demand-led: Reuters reported US regulators investigating 416,000 Tesla vehicles over unexpected braking [[n2033]] as Musk and Tesla attacked the SEC for unrelenting harassment [[n0892]]. Governance risk is being priced into the sector's largest weight, and Tesla is -12.04% over 20 sessions.
Narrative

Staples are where investors hide when they want inflation pass-through without growth risk. XLP rose 0.77% to 75.89 USD while the S&P 500 fell 2.12%, and Walmart gained 4.01% to 138.88 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17).
Reported

The New York Times reported Walmart's profits growing as consumers continue to spend [[n0973]], CNBC reported Walmart saying shoppers are on alert as grocery bills climb [[n0974]], and Modern Retail reported it gaining grocery share thanks to inflation [[n0971]]. ET Retail reported Kraft Heinz beating on raised prices and robust demand [[n0922]].
EPS Upside Watch

Brand power is being rewarded: Coca-Cola rose 2.00% to 62.12 USD and Procter & Gamble 1.15% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), after The Fiji Times reported Coca-Cola and PepsiCo warning of an inflation bite even as higher prices lift sales [[n1096]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The risk is the retailer, not the consumer: Reuters reported European retailers driving hard bargains with food giants [[n0898]]. Pricing power is migrating toward scale grocers such as Walmart, so own the shelf as well as the brand.
Narrative

Healthcare is defensive in aggregate but split by the pandemic cycle. XLV fell 1.61% to 128.47 USD and is -1.77% over 20 sessions, ahead of the S&P 500's -2.29% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17).
Reported

Moderna's CEO told CNBC it is reasonable to think the pandemic may be in its final stages [[n0765]], and Reuters reported Moderna eyeing a booster by August [[n0767]]. Moderna is -12.63% and Pfizer -9.53% over 20 sessions as COVID revenue visibility fades.
EPS Upside Watch

Pipelines carry the upside: Fierce Pharma reported Bristol Myers scoring FDA priority review for Breyanzi [[n1223]] and Bayer lifting Nubeqa's peak-sales goal to more than €3B [[n1222]]. AbbVie's +8.98% 20-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17) shows the rotation toward durable franchises.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Biotech funding is the stress point: STAT reported some newly public biotechs trading below cash [[n1881]], and XBI fell 4.27%. Below-cash valuations invite takeovers, so cash-rich acquirers hold the advantage. UnitedHealth Group's 2.02% fall to 470.34 USD shows even managed care did not escape the risk-off session.
Narrative

Materials are a barbell of real-asset winners and China-sensitive laggards. XLB fell 1.71% to 84.00 USD, yet Alcoa is +24.85%, CF Industries +18.49% and Mosaic +13.55% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17).
Reported

Barrick declared an increased dividend and a performance dividend policy [[n0714]], and Newmont rose 5.40% as gold climbed 1.63% to 1,902.00 USD/oz. Glencore reported record earnings while setting aside $1.5 billion for probes, Reuters reported [[n1157]].
EPS Upside Watch

Fertilisers carry the cleanest upside: MarketWatch argued the Russia-Ukraine crisis may make food-price inflation even worse [[n1977]], and wheat rose 2.24% to 798.00 US cents/bu (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Reuters reported Celanese nearing a deal of over $10 bln for a DuPont unit [[n0868]], so strategic buyers are paying up for specialty assets.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Gold miners are not chasing the metal: the Financial Post reported Barrick's CEO suggesting miners are overpaying for assets amid higher gold prices [[n0862]]. Capital discipline in a rising price tape is bullish for free cash flow.
Narrative

Listed real estate is paying for the rate move. XLRE fell 0.86% to 44.88 USD and is -4.35% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Realtor.com reported mortgage rates surging to their highest point since May 2019 [[n2168]].
Reported

Private capital is buying what public markets sell: The Real Deal reported Blackstone buying a multifamily REIT in a $5.8B deal [[n0718]], and WSJ reported Blackstone's European last-mile logistics deal valuing Mileway at $24 billion [[n0596]].
EPS Upside Watch

Rent growth is the offset: the Joint Center for Housing Studies reported rents soaring across the country while home prices grew even faster [[n0946]], and the San Francisco Fed asked whether rising rents will push up future inflation [[n2137]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Take-private bids set a floor under asset values even as listed REITs de-rate. If private buyers keep paying, the listed discount is an arbitrage rather than a warning, but only while credit markets stay open to leveraged buyers. Bloomberg reported Realty Income buying a Wynn Resorts Boston property for $1.7 billion [[n0697]], another sign that net-lease capital is still deploying.
Narrative

Utilities act as a bond proxy again on haven days. XLU edged up 0.06% to 66.34 USD as the S&P 500 fell 2.12%, but it remains -3.81% over 20 sessions while the 2Y rose 41 bps (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17; US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-17).
Reported
Southern Company CEO Tom Fanning told CNBC hybrid work is driving residential energy demand [[n0910]], while WABE reported the $30B Georgia Power nuclear plant delayed up to 6 more months [[n0833]].
EPS Upside Watch

Duke Energy is reshaping its rate base: E&E News reported plans to exit all coal and double renewables [[n0309]], and POWER Magazine reported a coal phaseout by 2035 [[n0885]]. Capex-driven rate-base growth is the earnings engine regulated utilities control.
⚡ Breaking Convention

NextEra's -9.74% 20-session slide against Duke Energy's -3.50% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17) shows the market charging most for long-dated growth even inside utilities; duration, not regulation, is the discount. Vistra's milder -1.10% 20-session move at 21.49 USD fits the same pattern, since a merchant generator carries less long-dated growth to discount.
Narrative

European autos are the cyclical that earnings keep rescuing. The STOXX 600 autos tracker (EXV5) closed at 62.19 EUR, +0.78% over five sessions but -3.72% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17).
Reported

Reuters reported Mercedes-Benz beating its profit forecast while flagging supply-chain headwinds in 2022 [[n0331]], and Bloomberg said Mercedes cars are more profitable than ever amid the chip shortage [[n1101]]; Mercedes-Benz Group is +9.05% over five sessions at 76.06 EUR. WSJ reported BMW taking control of its China venture and seeing big profit gains [[n0189]].
EPS Upside Watch

Volume recovery is the next leg: Reuters reported Volkswagen expecting the chip shortage to ease later in 2022 [[n0820]], and Mercedes-Benz's CFO saw supply-chain woes easing in the second half [[n0330]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Scarcity has been profitable because pricing replaced volume. Fortune argued a Russian invasion of Ukraine would make the chip shortage even worse [[n1952]], which would extend pricing but delay the volume recovery the bulls are counting on. Renault, +7.34% over 20 sessions at 36.34 EUR, shows the market still paying for restructuring stories in the meantime.
Narrative

Semiconductors are trading guidance and capex risk, not reported numbers. SOXX fell 3.76% to 471.84 USD and the PHLX Semiconductor Index 3.74% to 3,422.60 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17).
Reported

Nvidia announced fourth-quarter and fiscal 2022 results, per its newsroom [[n0141]], and Al Jazeera reported an upbeat current-quarter revenue forecast [[n1987]]; the stock still fell 7.56% to 245.07 USD. Reuters reported AMD closing its estimated $50 billion purchase of Xilinx [[n0445]].
EPS Upside Watch

Asian capacity is the next earnings leg: Asahi Shimbun reported TSMC expanding its Japan factory with Denso taking a stake [[n1573]], and SK Hynix is +4.72% over 20 sessions at 133,000.00 KRW. Intel agreed to acquire Tower Semiconductor for $5.4 billion [[n0612]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

ASML at 650.43 USD, -7.93% over 20 sessions, and TSMC's ADR at 119.76 USD, -6.68%, lag Nvidia's +1.48% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17): the equipment and foundry chain is priced for a capex peak that orders do not yet show. SOXL's 11.34% one-session drop shows how leveraged ETFs accelerate the selling.

earnings_pattern.title: Pricing power and cash returns rewarded; pandemic normalisation punished
parts: Rewarded

The rewarded group shares visible pricing power or cash returned to shareholders. Walmart rose 4.01% after WSJ reported it withstanding pandemic blows and higher costs to boost business [[n1240]]. Cisco gained 2.80% on a raised forecast and buybacks, and DoorDash closed +10.69% after CNBC reported record order numbers [[n0883]]. Airbnb is +6.78% over five sessions after Al Jazeera reported strong first-quarter revenue on a travel resurgence [[n0545]] (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). CNBC reported Coca-Cola beating estimates as demand for drinks away from home topped pre-pandemic levels [[n1087]], and the stock rose 2.00% on the risk-off day.
Punished

The punished group admitted normalisation or higher spending. CNBC reported Shopify closing down 16% after warning the pandemic boost will fade [[n0797]], and Roblox shares closing down 26% after an earnings miss [[n0791]]; Bloomberg called it Roblox's worst post-earnings drop, wrecking the stock-pop narrative [[n0144]]. Reuters reported Palantir's margins taking a hit from higher spending in its commercial push [[n0941]], and the stock fell 15.75%. Nvidia slid 7.56% the day after its fourth-quarter report [[n1226]] (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17).
Pattern

Beats are table stakes; the market is grading the second derivative. A company that says growth will slow, as Al Jazeera reported of Shopify's weaker outlook [[n1996]], or whose sales were hurt by the COVID decline, as The Boston Globe reported of Roblox and Shopify [[n1203]], is de-rated even when the quarter is fine. Companies that convert inflation into revenue, such as Walmart with what Bloomberg called a cart full of reasons to love inflation [[n0970]], or that return cash, such as Cisco, are re-rated. Rising discount rates make the distant part of a growth story worth less, so any hint of delay is punished disproportionately.
Attention into EPS

Attention is concentrated in the punished cohort. Bloomberg reported Cathie Wood's ARKK a year from its peak and still struggling [[n1868]], and ARKK fell 6.44% to 68.18 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), while CNBC reported Wood calling her innovation stocks way undervalued [[n1889]]. Crowded conviction into conservative guides magnifies the downside on the print.
Playbook

Action: buy post-earnings strength only where guidance carries pricing power or buybacks, and fade relief rallies in pandemic beneficiaries that guide to normalisation. Trigger: a beat-and-raise with stable margins. What changes the call: a VIX retreat below its 20-session-earlier 25.59 index points would let the market reward growth again and narrow the penalty for cautious guidance.

underowned.title: Fertiliser and grain chain: CF Industries, Nutrien, Mosaic
parts: Attention Gap

Fertiliser equities have rallied quietly, with CF Industries +18.49%, Mosaic +13.55% and Nutrien +7.20% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), while attention sits on oil and gold. Al Jazeera's infographic on Russia, Ukraine and the global wheat supply [[n2023]] frames a crop-input story few equity screens track.
Exposure & Risk

Grain prices already embed a premium: soybeans at 1,592.00 US cents/bu are +11.66% over 20 sessions and corn at 650.00 US cents/bu +6.38% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Farm Policy News examined Ukrainian corn and wheat export flows [[n1959]]. Nutrien still rose 2.81% to 77.17 USD on the risk-off session. The risk is speed: de-escalation would deflate the premium faster than earnings could rise.
Trigger to Watch
Any disruption to Black Sea grain shipments, or wheat breaking higher from 798.00 US cents/bu.

underowned.title: Japan chip equipment: Tokyo Electron and Advantest
parts: Attention Gap

While US semis sold off, Tokyo Electron rose 3.72% and Advantest 4.50% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). The Economist argued Japan's Automation Inc is indispensable to global industry [[n1552]], yet global attention stays on US chip designers. Bottleneck suppliers hold the same pricing power investors are rewarding elsewhere.
Exposure & Risk

Both remain below their 20-session-earlier levels, Tokyo Electron -5.47% and Advantest -4.41%, so the rebound is early. The risk is a global capex pause; SMH fell 4.01% on the last US session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), and Reuters reported Taiwan moving to boost protection for its semiconductor secrets [[n0801]], a reminder that technology controls can shift.
Trigger to Watch
Tokyo Electron reclaiming its 20-session-earlier 61,590.00 JPY would confirm leadership.

underowned.title: Nuclear fuel and SMRs: Cameco, Centrus Energy, URA
parts: Attention Gap

Policy momentum toward nuclear power is building: Forbes reported France vowing to build more nuclear energy after high gas prices [[n1967]], and POWER Magazine reported Poland securing a NuScale SMR [[n1605]]. Yet Cameco fell 6.07% over five sessions to 21.04 USD and URA is -4.25% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). The driver is the same gas shock lifting LNG, but equities have not linked the two.
Exposure & Risk

Centrus Energy at 42.10 USD is -6.15% over five sessions. These are small, volatile names that risk-off selling hits first, project lead times run for years, and policy support can stall at the permitting stage.
Trigger to Watch
Procurement news: Parkiet reported Sasin and KGHM heading to the US for small nuclear technology [[n1706]]. Signed supply contracts would convert policy into revenue.

underowned.title: US natural gas and LNG export supply
parts: Attention Gap

Henry Hub at 4.49 USD/MMBtu is +17.99% over 20 sessions and +13.31% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), while attention is on crude. The EIA forecast US marketed natural gas production rising in 2022 and 2023 [[n2034]], volume growth few investors connect to Europe's shortage.
Exposure & Risk

The EIA noted Europe relies primarily on imports to meet its natural gas needs [[n1910]], and TTF at 74.91 EUR/MWh keeps the transatlantic spread wide. ConocoPhillips at 91.16 USD is +6.46% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Risk: a mild end to winter, or a Russian supply guarantee that collapses the European premium.
Trigger to Watch
Long-term contracts: Reuters reported Beijing Gas in talks over a 10-year Shell LNG deal [[n0863]]; signings validate export capacity and lock in volumes.

crypto.title: Bitcoin trades as Nasdaq beta, not digital gold
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin fell 7.79% to 40,538.01 USD on its latest completed day and is -4.04% over five sessions, though still +7.29% over 20 sessions from 37,784.33 USD; Ether fell 7.88% to 2,881.48 USD and Solana 8.36% to 93.41 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-17). The same day gold rose 1.63% and the Nasdaq 100 fell 2.96% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), so crypto traded with growth equities rather than with havens. Equity proxies amplified the move, with Coinbase Global -7.71%, Marathon Digital -9.44% and GBTC -8.93%. CNBC had laid out the outlook for bitcoin as geopolitical tensions heat up and interest rates rise [[n2202]], and both forces are now working against it.
New / Most Important

Regulatory scrutiny is rising alongside institutional capital. The Financial Stability Board warned of emerging risks from crypto-assets to global financial stability [[n1053]]. At the same time, Forbes reported Sequoia launching a $500 million fund to invest in crypto tokens [[n1067]], Ledger Insights reported stablecoin firm Circle doubling its valuation to $9 billion in a new SPAC deal [[n1398]], and Fortune noted Warren Buffett investing $1 billion in a crypto-friendly bank [[n0828]]. Capital is flowing to infrastructure and stablecoins, not to spot tokens. The Super Bowl marketing blitz has not converted: The Seattle Times reported the crypto ad millions did not drive downloads [[n0113]], WIRED said the ads felt like Pets.com all over again [[n0094]], and Business Insider reported Charlie Munger slamming crypto while ringing an inflation alarm [[n0869]].
Playbook

Action: keep crypto exposure light and treat it as high-beta growth rather than a hedge. Trigger to add: Bitcoin holding its level on a day the Nasdaq 100 falls, the first evidence of decoupling. What changes the call: a daily close back below the 20-session-earlier 37,784.33 USD would erase the bounce and argue for cutting miners and exchange equity first.

flows.title: Liquidity tightening at the margin; havens absorb the flows
parts: Global Liquidity

Liquidity is being withdrawn on two fronts, rate expectations and balance-sheet plans. Reuters examined what could drive the Fed to a Plan B for balance-sheet reduction [[n1399]], and The Economist argued that quantitative tightening is no substitute for higher interest rates [[n2184]]. Europe is withdrawing support more slowly, with Lagarde pledging only a gradual policy shift, as Reuters reported [[n1308]]. China is the counterweight, with Bloomberg reporting the PBOC pumping in more liquidity [[n0228]], but that liquidity stays largely onshore. Market plumbing is the amplifier: Bloomberg reported Treasury market liquidity eroding with the Fed's course a gamble [[n2214]]. The net effect is fewer marginal buyers of risk on down days and larger gaps when news breaks outside US hours.
Rates & Dollar

The front end is absorbing haven demand. The 2Y is down 12 bps and the 10Y down 6 bps over five observations, with the 3M bill at 0.36% and the 10Y-3M spread at +161 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-17). TLT rose 0.74% and IEF 0.54% on the session, while the US Dollar Index (DXY) sits at 95.80 index points, +0.26% over five sessions and +0.06% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Reuters reported the dollar gaining as Ukraine worries rose and Bullard reiterated his rate comments [[n0114]], and Reuters separately reported the yuan slipping on divergent China-US policy [[n0244]]. The spillover runs through emerging markets: a Mexican central bank official told Reuters that Fed hikes will limit Mexico's monetary policy [[n2230]], and EMB is -1.97% over 20 sessions.
Credit Check

Credit is leaking, not breaking. HYG is -3.11% and LQD -3.65% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), and the high-yield ETF slipped 0.42% on a day the long-bond ETF rallied. Reuters reported global companies slowing debt-raising as yields climb [[n1386]], which removes supply but also signals issuers are unwilling to pay the new price. In Europe, Reuters argued the ECB put for euro zone bond markets is some way off [[n1281]], so periphery spreads lack a backstop. In China, Bloomberg's report that Cedar could not pay $3.1 billion overdue [[n0218]] keeps offshore high yield untouchable. Artemis reported insurance-linked bonds showing resilience as spreads reset [[n1378]], evidence that uncorrelated credit holds while corporate spreads drift wider.
Equity & Fund Flows

Corporate buybacks remain the most dependable bid, led by the $15 bln Cisco programme Reuters reported [[n1184]]. Large investors are rotating, per 13F disclosures: Business Insider reported Stanley Druckenmiller dumped Meta before its $230 billion wipeout [[n0661]], Reuters reported George Soros buying a stake in Rivian [[n0454]], and City AM reported Berkshire Hathaway dumping Visa and Mastercard stock while buying $1bn of Nubank [[n0822]]. The Straits Times reported Temasek adding stakes in Grab, Robinhood and other consumer-focused companies [[n1862]]. Protection is in demand: Bloomberg reported a big options trade hedging an S&P 500 plunge of up to 20% by April [[n2200]], and STOXX reported increased VSTOXX futures activity amid the pullback [[n1355]]. Primary markets are open but selective: Reuters reported SPACs discussing a $20-bln deal for Allied Universal [[n1375]], and CNBC reported India's Life Insurance Corporation filing for an $8 billion IPO [[n1371]], a large supply event for emerging-market equity allocators.
Portfolio Implication

Position for scarce liquidity: hold short-duration Treasuries for the haven bid, overweight energy and staples for inflation pass-through, and keep a gold sleeve; the GDX miners ETF rose 13.33% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Stay underweight high yield against investment grade until issuance resumes, and keep emerging-market debt light while the dollar is firm. Re-risk only when two signals align, HYG stabilising and the VIX closing below its 20-session-earlier 25.59 index points. If the 2Y resumes its climb while credit keeps leaking, the market is pricing policy error; then cut equity beta further.

anticipatory.title: Munich weekend: diplomatic channel versus military move
parts: What Is Priced

The Munich Security Conference opens without Russia, the event chair told Reuters [[n0119]], and the conference's own site showed the venue on the eve of MSC 2022 [[n0153]]. Markets are already priced for stress: the VIX at 28.11 index points, gold at 1,902.00 USD/oz and the 2Y down 12 bps over five observations (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17; US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-17).
Conditional Expression

If Munich produces a credible diplomatic channel, take profit on gold and GDX and rotate into beaten-down European banks such as Societe Generale, -10.30% over five sessions. If shelling escalates, after The Guardian reported separatist shelling raising tensions in east Ukraine [[n1521]], add to energy through XLE and defence through ITA and keep the front-end Treasury hedge.
Risk

Weekend gap risk dominates: news can break with markets shut, and the Atlantic Council assessed that an invasion could come with less than 12 hours' notice [[n1620]]. Size positions for gaps, not stops.

anticipatory.title: Deere's print and the farm-capex test
parts: What Is Priced

Deere closed at 380.53 USD, -2.57% on the session but +3.69% over 20 sessions, into results that Barron's said are coming Friday [[n0150]]. Crop prices underpin farm incomes, with corn at 650.00 US cents/bu and soybeans at 1,592.00 US cents/bu (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). The same farm-income cycle has lifted CF Industries to 76.19 USD, +2.38% on the session, so Deere is the downstream read on whether growers are spending that income on equipment.
Conditional Expression

If Deere shows pricing outrunning steel and freight costs, pair long Deere against Caterpillar, -10.10% over 20 sessions, expressing farm over construction capex. If margins compress despite demand, apply the Palantir template and fade the first bounce.
Risk

Freight is the margin threat: WSJ reported expensive shipping containers meaning rough sailing for global trade [[n2019]]. Crop prices could also cool, as Successful Farming reported a dry South American soybean crop looking to improve with rain [[n1980]], which would trim the farm-income tailwind.

anticipatory.title: March lift-off: 25 or 50 basis points
parts: What Is Priced

A Reuters poll had the Fed raising rates 25 bps in March while calls for 50 bps grow louder [[n1376]]. The 2Y at 1.49% is +41 bps over 20 observations on a curve that is positively sloped and bear flattening (both up, 2Y up more) (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-17). The five-observation 12 bps fall in the 2Y shows the haven bid has trimmed some of the hawkish premium.
Conditional Expression

If more officials echo Bullard's call for a front-loaded campaign, as WSJ reported [[n1392]], sell the 2Y and add curve flatteners while keeping growth equities underweight. If the Ukraine shock dominates and the Fed signals a measured start, the curve can re-steepen, favouring banks over utilities.
Risk

Minutes showing a Fed not wed to a set pace, as Reuters reported [[n2223]], mean data can swing the debate quickly; Reuters reported consumer prices posting the largest annual gain in 40 years [[n2118]], and another hot print would revive the case for a larger first move.

anticipatory.title: Iran deal versus Saudi restraint
parts: What Is Priced

Brent closed at 92.97 USD/bbl, -1.94% on the session but +5.19% over 20, with WTI at 91.76 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), as Reuters reported the US in the very final stages of Iran nuclear talks [[n1501]]. The market is pricing some deal probability without pricing new barrels soon.
Conditional Expression

A signed deal would pressure crude and lift refiners and airlines; Reuters reported Asian refiners eager to resume Iranian oil imports as high prices bite [[n2011]]. No deal plus escalation in Ukraine fits the case Bloomberg made that oil's Covid crash set the world up for $100 crude [[n0142]]; then add XLE and USO.
Risk

Saudi restraint limits any offset: The Intercept reported Saudi Arabia rejecting Biden's plea to increase oil production as midterms loom [[n1971]]. The draft's oil-later sequencing, which Reuters detailed [[n1514]], makes a deal less bearish for crude than headlines imply, so short-crude expressions need a signed text, not optimism.

catalysts.title: Walmart (WMT): grocery share gains as the inflation hedge
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Walmart is converting inflation into traffic. Al Jazeera reported it thriving despite supply-chain woes and high inflation [[n0972]], and Reuters reported its Mexico unit lifting profit 5% even as costs increased [[n1211]]. Scale lets Walmart hold price gaps that smaller grocers cannot, and grocery share is the stickiest form of revenue.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock rose 4.01% to 138.88 USD but remains below its 20-session-earlier 141.22 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Risk: CNBC reported shoppers on alert as grocery bills climb [[n0974]], and trade-down could squeeze mix.
Trade Expression
Buy on a close above 141.22 USD, paired against Target, -7.99% over 20 sessions, to isolate scale. Cut if the stock gives back its results-day gain.

catalysts.title: Cisco (CSCO): beat, raise and buy back
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

CNBC's Investing Club described Cisco defying the doubters with a beat and raise [[n1196]], and the buyback adds a dependable bid. WSJ reported a $20 billion-plus takeover offer for Splunk [[n1097]], showing management will use the balance sheet to buy recurring software revenue. Hardware with visible orders is the rewarded profile on this tape.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Cisco rose 2.80% to 55.77 USD but is -3.98% over 20 sessions against a 20-session-earlier 58.08 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Risk: a large acquisition at a premium would dilute buyback capacity.
Trade Expression
Accumulate below 58.08 USD and add on a close above it. Reassess if a Splunk deal comes with a premium that crowds out repurchases.

catalysts.title: Nvidia (NVDA): upbeat guide, sold anyway
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Nvidia announced fourth-quarter and fiscal 2022 results [[n0141]] and, per Al Jazeera, forecast upbeat current-quarter revenue [[n1987]]. The franchise is intact; the problem is a valuation that already discounted the beat, in a tape that punishes duration. Competition is rising too, after Reuters reported AMD closing its estimated $50 billion Xilinx purchase [[n0445]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock fell 7.56% to 245.07 USD, close to its 20-session-earlier 241.50 USD and still +1.48% over that span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Risk: AMD's 4.52% fall the same day shows the whole complex de-rating together.
Trade Expression
Wait: buy only on a hold above 241.50 USD with the SOX stabilising. A close below that level would put the stock negative over 20 sessions and argue for patience.

catalysts.title: Intel (INTC): the comeback plan needs proof
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Bloomberg reported Intel's CEO tired of Wall Street doubting his comeback plan [[n1195]], and The New York Times asked whether Intel can make a comeback as the world needs what it makes [[n0960]]. Tom's Hardware reported AMD's market cap surpassing Intel's for the first time in history [[n0540]], the scoreboard investors are watching. Intel's agreed $5.4 billion purchase of Tower Semiconductor [[n0612]] adds foundry capacity to the plan.
Price Hurdle & Risk
Intel fell 1.37% to 47.57 USD and is -8.59% over 20 sessions from 52.04 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Risk: heavy capex delays free cash flow for years.
Trade Expression
Hold a starter position; add on a close above 52.04 USD. Cut if foundry milestones slip.

catalysts.title: Palantir (PLTR): commercial push, margin pain
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Reuters reported that Palantir's margins will take a hit from higher spending in its commercial push [[n0941]]. In a market paying for near-term cash, management chose growth spending over margin, and investors repriced the stock immediately. Peers confirm the pattern: C3.ai fell 9.55% and Snowflake 6.05% on the same session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17).
Price Hurdle & Risk

Palantir fell 15.75% to 11.77 USD and is -19.49% over 20 sessions from 14.62 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Risk to the bearish view: a short-covering bounce in a stock this heavily sold.
Trade Expression
Stay underweight; reassess only on a close back above 14.62 USD or evidence that commercial wins are lifting operating leverage.

catalysts.title: Deere (DE): farm pricing versus freight costs
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Barron's previewed Deere's earnings, which it said are coming Friday [[n0150]]. Strong crop prices support farm incomes, with soybeans +11.66% and corn +6.38% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), and the open question is whether Deere's pricing outruns steel, freight and labour costs.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Deere fell 2.57% to 380.53 USD but is +3.69% over 20 sessions from 366.98 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), outperforming Caterpillar's -10.10%. Risk: a margin miss would follow the market's pattern of punishing spending, whatever the order book shows.
Trade Expression
Wait for the print. Buy a close above 380.53 USD on confirmed price realisation; avoid below 366.98 USD, where the 20-session outperformance would be gone.
